title: Head & Neck Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for squamous-cell head and neck cancer. Full pathway by subsite (oral cavity, oropharynx with HPV/p16 status, larynx/hypopharynx, nasopharynx), then workup -> AJCC staging / risk stratification -> early single-modality vs locally advanced treatment, with every locally advanced arm refined THROUGH a response / restaging decision (post-chemoradiation restaging, induction response, larynx-preservation selection, EBV-DNA-guided adjuvant) before the next step, curative arms routing surgery -> risk-directed adjuvant -> surveillance and definitive chemoradiation -> restaging -> surveillance or salvage. Recurrent / metastatic disease carries a line-of-therapy sub-tree (first line by PD-L1 CPS -> on progression -> second line -> later line / best supportive care). Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; surgery, radiation, and regimens without a dose protocol (induction TPF, gemcitabine-cisplatin) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Invents no dose/regimen/criterion. Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references; no proprietary guideline text reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard guidelines (NCCN Head and Neck Cancers, DeVita, Harrison). Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: High-risk pathologic features after resection - extranodal (extracapsular) extension and/or a positive surgical margin - are the accepted indications for adding concurrent cisplatin to postoperative radiation. Other adverse features (multiple positive nodes, perineural/lymphovascular invasion, pT3-4, close margin) favor postoperative radiation alone.

b.text: HPV/p16 status is prognostic in oropharyngeal cancer (p16-positive disease carries a markedly better prognosis) and drives 8th-edition staging, but treatment de-escalation for p16-positive disease remains investigational - treat to standard intensity off-protocol.

c.text: In first-line recurrent/metastatic disease, PD-L1 CPS guides checkpoint-inhibitor selection: pembrolizumab monotherapy for CPS >= 1 (favored in lower-burden disease), pembrolizumab + platinum + 5-FU for any CPS (favored for higher tumor burden or rapid progression), and platinum + 5-FU + cetuximab (EXTREME) when immunotherapy is not suitable.

d.text: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is a distinct entity (EBV-associated, chemoradiation-sensitive, not surgically resected as primary therapy). Plasma EBV DNA aids prognosis, response assessment, and post-treatment monitoring; a detectable level after chemoradiation supports adjuvant chemotherapy.

e.text: Response-adapted sequencing: after definitive chemoradiation, restage (clinical exam plus PET-CT ~12 weeks after treatment) - a complete response goes to surveillance, isolated residual nodal disease is addressed with neck dissection, and persistent/progressive primary disease is managed as recurrent/metastatic. After induction chemotherapy (e.g. TPF), a response supports proceeding to radiation-based local therapy while a poor response redirects to surgery.

nodes.name: Subsite
nodes.title: Primary subsite / presentation
nodes.description: Squamous-cell head and neck cancer management branches first by primary subsite; nasopharynx is a distinct entity. Select the anatomic site, or enter directly at the recurrent/metastatic pathway.
bullets: Oral cavity (lip, tongue, floor of mouth, buccal mucosa, gingiva, hard palate)
Oropharynx (tonsil, base of tongue, soft palate) - test HPV/p16
Larynx / hypopharynx
Nasopharynx (EBV-associated, distinct pathway)
Recurrent or metastatic disease (enter the systemic pathway)

nodes.name: Oral cavity workup
nodes.title: Oral cavity: workup
nodes.description: Confirm squamous histology, define local extent (bone, depth of invasion) and nodal/distant status.
bullets: History and physical incl. complete head-and-neck exam and dental evaluation; biopsy confirming squamous-cell carcinoma
Contrast CT and/or MRI of primary and neck; assess mandibular/maxillary bone invasion and depth of invasion
Chest imaging; PET-CT for stage III-IVB or clinically node-positive disease to exclude distant metastases / second primary
Examination under anesthesia / panendoscopy as indicated; nutrition, speech-and-swallow, and smoking-cessation assessment
Multidisciplinary tumor-board review before treatment

nodes.name: Oropharynx workup
nodes.title: Oropharynx: workup (incl. HPV/p16)
nodes.description: Standard head-and-neck workup plus HPV/p16 testing, which is prognostic and determines staging.
bullets: Biopsy confirming squamous-cell carcinoma; p16 immunohistochemistry (surrogate for HPV) on tumor or nodal metastasis
Contrast CT/MRI of primary and neck; PET-CT for staging and to identify an occult primary in nodal presentations
Chest imaging; dental, nutrition, and speech-and-swallow evaluation
For cystic neck node with unknown primary - HPV/p16 testing of the node points to an oropharyngeal origin
Multidisciplinary tumor-board review

nodes.name: Larynx/hypopharynx workup
nodes.title: Larynx / hypopharynx: workup
nodes.description: Define primary extent and laryngeal function to inform organ-preservation vs surgical options.
bullets: Biopsy confirming squamous-cell carcinoma; laryngoscopy documenting vocal-cord mobility and airway
Contrast CT/MRI of primary and neck; assess cartilage invasion and pre-epiglottic/paraglottic spread
Chest imaging; PET-CT for stage III-IVB or node-positive disease
Baseline speech-and-swallow and pulmonary assessment (relevant to laryngectomy vs preservation)
Multidisciplinary tumor-board review

nodes.name: Nasopharynx workup
nodes.title: Nasopharynx: workup (incl. EBV)
nodes.description: Distinct EBV-associated entity - nasopharyngeal-specific imaging and EBV testing.
bullets: Nasopharyngeal endoscopy and biopsy; WHO histologic type
MRI of nasopharynx and skull base (superior for perineural/intracranial extent) plus neck; PET-CT for regional/distant staging
Plasma EBV DNA (prognostic and used for response assessment and post-treatment monitoring)
Audiometry, dental, nutrition, and thyroid/pituitary baseline (radiation field considerations)
Multidisciplinary tumor-board review

nodes.name: Oral cavity stage
nodes.title: Oral cavity: stage / risk stratification
nodes.description: Group by AJCC stage. Early (I-II) disease is treated with a single modality; locally advanced (III-IVB) disease needs combined-modality therapy.

nodes.name: Oropharynx p16
nodes.title: Oropharynx: HPV/p16 status
nodes.description: p16 status determines the AJCC staging system and prognosis for oropharyngeal cancer.

nodes.name: Oropharynx p16+ stage
nodes.title: Oropharynx (p16+): stage grouping
nodes.description: p16-positive oropharyngeal cancer uses a distinct, more favorable staging system - many node-positive tumors are stage I-II.

tables.title: p16-positive oropharynx clinical stage (8th ed., simplified)
rows: Node-positive can still be stage I

nodes.name: Oropharynx p16- stage
nodes.title: Oropharynx (p16-): stage grouping
nodes.description: p16-negative oropharyngeal cancer follows HPV-independent staging and behaves like other mucosal squamous cancers.

nodes.name: Larynx stage
nodes.title: Larynx / hypopharynx: stage / risk stratification
nodes.description: Group by AJCC stage. Early disease is treated with a single modality; locally advanced disease is managed with organ-preservation or surgical strategies.

nodes.name: Nasopharynx stage
nodes.title: Nasopharynx: stage grouping
nodes.description: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is treated non-surgically. Stage I is radiation alone; higher stages need chemoradiation with or without induction/adjuvant chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Oral cavity early
nodes.title: Oral cavity, early (I-II): surgery, then pathology review
nodes.description: Single-modality surgery, then final pathology decides whether risk-directed adjuvant therapy is needed.
bullets: Wide surgical excision of the primary to negative margins, with neck dissection (elective for depth of invasion beyond a few mm or clinically node-positive)
Definitive radiation is an alternative when surgery would cause major functional loss or the patient is inoperable
Review final pathology for adverse features, then proceed to the postoperative risk-stratification step
No routine systemic therapy for truly early, fully resected, low-risk disease

nodes.name: Oropharynx early
nodes.title: Oropharynx, early (I-II): single modality
nodes.description: Early oropharyngeal cancer is treated with a single modality - definitive radiation or transoral surgery.
bullets: Definitive radiation to primary and neck, OR transoral (TORS) resection with neck dissection
Choice balances functional outcome (swallow, xerostomia) and patient factors; treat p16-positive disease to standard intensity (de-escalation is investigational)
If surgery reveals adverse pathology, add risk-directed adjuvant therapy
Elective nodal coverage/dissection given the high rate of occult nodal disease

nodes.name: Larynx early
nodes.title: Larynx / hypopharynx, early (I-II): single modality
nodes.description: Early laryngeal cancer is treated with a single modality aimed at voice preservation.
bullets: Definitive radiation OR endoscopic/transoral laser resection (glottic T1-2), with comparable local control
Partial laryngectomy in selected patients
Choice driven by voice outcome, tumor location, and follow-up feasibility
No routine systemic therapy for early, single-modality disease

nodes.name: Nasopharynx early
nodes.title: Nasopharynx, stage I: radiation alone
nodes.description: Early nasopharyngeal carcinoma is treated with definitive radiation alone.
bullets: Definitive intensity-modulated radiation to the nasopharynx and elective neck
No concurrent chemotherapy for true stage I disease
Post-treatment plasma EBV DNA and imaging for monitoring

nodes.name: Oral cavity LA approach
nodes.title: Oral cavity, locally advanced: primary approach
nodes.description: Resectable oral-cavity cancer is treated with surgery first, then risk-directed adjuvant therapy. Unresectable disease is treated with definitive concurrent chemoradiation.
nodes.path: Head & Neck / Oral cavity / LA / Approach

nodes.name: Oropharynx LA approach
nodes.title: Oropharynx, locally advanced: primary approach
nodes.description: Locally advanced oropharyngeal cancer is managed by concurrent chemoradiation, induction chemotherapy followed by radiation, or transoral surgery with risk-directed adjuvant therapy.

nodes.name: Larynx LA approach
nodes.title: Larynx / hypopharynx, locally advanced: organ preservation vs surgery
nodes.description: Locally advanced laryngeal/hypopharyngeal cancer is managed by concurrent chemoradiation (organ preservation), induction chemotherapy to select responders, or total laryngectomy with adjuvant therapy. Extensive T4a cartilage destruction favors upfront laryngectomy.

nodes.name: Nasopharynx LA approach
nodes.title: Nasopharynx, stage II-IVA: chemoradiation strategy
nodes.description: Concurrent cisplatin-radiation is the backbone; higher-stage / bulky disease adds induction chemotherapy before chemoradiation.

options.label: Induction chemotherapy, then chemoradiation (stage III-IVA / bulky)

nodes.name: Oral cavity LA definitive CRT
nodes.title: Oral cavity, unresectable: definitive concurrent chemoradiation
nodes.description: Definitive radiation with concurrent cisplatin for unresectable or inoperable locally advanced disease, then response-adapted restaging.
nodes.path: Head & Neck / Oral cavity / LA / Definitive CRT
bullets: Definitive radiation to the primary and neck with concurrent high-dose cisplatin
Cetuximab-radiation is an alternative when cisplatin is contraindicated (less effective than cisplatin)
Restage after treatment; residual nodal disease is addressed surgically (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Oropharynx LA chemoRT
nodes.title: Oropharynx, LA: concurrent chemoradiation
nodes.description: Definitive radiation with concurrent high-dose cisplatin - the standard organ-preserving option - then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Definitive radiation to primary and neck with concurrent high-dose cisplatin
Cetuximab-radiation if cisplatin is contraindicated (inferior to cisplatin, particularly in p16-positive disease)
Restage after treatment; neck dissection for residual nodal disease (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Larynx LA chemoRT
nodes.title: Larynx / hypopharynx, LA: concurrent chemoradiation
nodes.description: Concurrent cisplatin-radiation preserves the larynx in appropriately selected locally advanced disease, then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Definitive radiation with concurrent high-dose cisplatin for larynx preservation
Cetuximab-radiation if cisplatin is contraindicated
Total laryngectomy reserved for salvage of persistent/recurrent disease or a non-functional larynx
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Nasopharynx CRT
nodes.title: Nasopharynx, stage II-IVA: concurrent chemoradiation
nodes.description: Concurrent high-dose cisplatin with definitive radiation, then EBV-DNA-guided restaging.
bullets: Concurrent high-dose cisplatin with definitive intensity-modulated radiation
Elective irradiation of bilateral neck given the high nodal-involvement rate
Post-treatment plasma EBV DNA guides whether adjuvant chemotherapy is added (next step)
Concurrent cisplatin-radiation regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Nasopharynx induction + CRT
nodes.title: Nasopharynx, stage III-IVA: induction, then chemoradiation
nodes.description: Induction chemotherapy for bulky disease, followed by concurrent cisplatin-radiation, then EBV-DNA-guided restaging.
nodes.path: Head & Neck / Nasopharynx / LA / Induction + CRT
bullets: Induction gemcitabine + cisplatin (or docetaxel/cisplatin/5-FU) before chemoradiation for stage III-IVA / bulky nodal disease
Then concurrent high-dose cisplatin with definitive radiation
Post-treatment plasma EBV DNA guides adjuvant chemotherapy (next step)
Concurrent cisplatin-radiation and induction gemcitabine-cisplatin regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Oropharynx LA induction
nodes.title: Oropharynx, LA: induction chemotherapy
nodes.description: Induction chemotherapy for selected high-burden disease, then response-adapted local therapy.
bullets: Induction docetaxel + cisplatin + 5-FU (TPF) for very bulky nodal disease or when rapid response is needed
Not shown superior to concurrent chemoradiation given upfront; requires good performance status and close toxicity monitoring
Assess response, then proceed to radiation-based local therapy or surgery (next step)
Induction TPF regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Induction response
nodes.title: Response to induction chemotherapy
nodes.description: Response to induction chemotherapy directs the local modality - a response supports radiation-based therapy; poor response or progression redirects to surgery.

options.label: Response - proceed to radiation-based local therapy

nodes.name: Post-induction chemoRT
nodes.title: After induction (responder): radiation-based local therapy
nodes.description: Responders proceed to definitive radiation with a concurrent systemic agent, then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Definitive radiation with a concurrent systemic agent (cisplatin, or carboplatin/cetuximab if cisplatin unsuitable)
Then restage; residual nodal disease is addressed surgically (next step)
De-intensification after induction remains investigational - treat to standard intensity
Concurrent cisplatin-radiation regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Post-induction surgery
nodes.title: After induction (poor response): surgery + risk-directed adjuvant
nodes.description: Non-responders proceed to surgical resection with subsequent risk-directed adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Surgical resection of the primary and neck when technically feasible
Definitive chemoradiation if unresectable after induction
Then postoperative risk stratification directs adjuvant therapy (next step)
Surgery has no dose protocol - checklist guidance only

nodes.name: Larynx LA induction
nodes.title: Larynx / hypopharynx, LA: induction (preservation selection)
nodes.description: Induction chemotherapy selects responders for larynx-preserving radiation; the laryngeal response is assessed next.
bullets: Induction docetaxel + cisplatin + 5-FU (TPF) as a larynx-preservation selection strategy
Assess laryngeal response after induction (next step)
Requires good performance status and reliable follow-up
Induction TPF regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Larynx induction response
nodes.title: Larynx: response to induction (preservation decision)
nodes.description: Laryngeal response to induction chemotherapy decides preservation versus laryngectomy.

options.label: Good laryngeal response - preserve with radiation

nodes.name: Larynx preservation RT
nodes.title: Larynx (responder): definitive radiation for preservation
nodes.description: Good responders proceed to larynx-preserving radiation with a concurrent systemic agent, then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: Definitive radiation with a concurrent systemic agent for larynx preservation
Then restage; salvage laryngectomy for persistent/recurrent disease
Neck dissection for residual nodal disease (next step)
Concurrent cisplatin-radiation regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Total laryngectomy
nodes.title: Larynx (poor response / T4a): total laryngectomy + adjuvant
nodes.description: Total laryngectomy for poor induction response or extensive cartilage destruction, followed by risk-directed adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Total laryngectomy with neck dissection and appropriate reconstruction / voice rehabilitation
Extensive T4a cartilage destruction favors upfront laryngectomy over preservation
Then postoperative risk stratification directs adjuvant therapy (next step)
Surgery has no dose protocol - checklist guidance only

nodes.name: Post-CRT restaging
nodes.title: Restaging after definitive chemoradiation
nodes.description: Restage ~12 weeks after chemoradiation (clinical exam plus PET-CT). Response directs whether the patient goes to surveillance, neck dissection, or salvage for persistent disease.

nodes.name: CRT complete response
nodes.title: Complete response after chemoradiation: surveillance
nodes.description: A complete response after chemoradiation proceeds to structured surveillance.
bullets: No planned neck dissection when PET-CT confirms a complete nodal response
Proceed to structured surveillance (next step)
Address late radiation toxicity (xerostomia, dysphagia, hypothyroidism) proactively

nodes.name: Post-CRT neck dissection
nodes.title: Residual nodal disease: neck dissection
nodes.description: Isolated residual nodal disease after chemoradiation is treated with neck dissection.
bullets: Neck dissection for residual or PET-avid nodal disease with a controlled primary
Then structured surveillance (next step)
Surgery has no dose protocol - checklist guidance only

nodes.name: Persistent after CRT
nodes.title: Persistent / progressive primary: manage as recurrent disease
nodes.description: Persistent or progressive primary disease after chemoradiation is managed on the recurrent / metastatic pathway.
bullets: Assess resectability of the persistent primary for salvage surgery
Unresectable persistent disease is treated with systemic therapy (recurrent / metastatic pathway, next step)
Consider clinical trials

nodes.name: Adjuvant risk
nodes.title: Postoperative risk stratification
nodes.description: After resection, adverse pathology determines adjuvant therapy. Extranodal extension or a positive margin (high risk) calls for concurrent chemoradiation; other adverse features favor radiation alone; none favors observation.

tables.title: Postoperative adverse features and adjuvant therapy
rows: pT3-4, N2-3, perineural/lymphovascular invasion, close margin
None of the above, negative margins

options.label: High risk (extranodal extension and/or positive margin)

nodes.name: Adjuvant chemoRT
nodes.title: Adjuvant: concurrent chemoradiation (high risk)
nodes.description: High-risk pathology - postoperative radiation with concurrent cisplatin, then surveillance.
bullets: Postoperative radiation with concurrent high-dose cisplatin
Start radiation promptly (ideally within ~6 weeks of surgery)
Cisplatin alternatives (e.g. weekly cisplatin, carboplatin) if high-dose cisplatin not tolerated
Then structured surveillance (next step); regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant RT
nodes.title: Adjuvant: radiation alone (intermediate risk)
nodes.description: Intermediate-risk pathology without extranodal extension or positive margin - postoperative radiation alone, then surveillance.
bullets: Postoperative radiation to the tumor bed and at-risk nodal levels
No concurrent chemotherapy in the absence of extranodal extension or a positive margin
Reassess for concurrent chemotherapy if final review reclassifies risk upward
Then structured surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Adjuvant observation
nodes.title: Adjuvant: observation (low risk)
nodes.description: Fully resected, negative-margin, low-risk disease proceeds to surveillance without adjuvant therapy.
bullets: No adjuvant radiation or chemotherapy for negative-margin disease without adverse features
Then structured surveillance (next step)
Re-review pathology if any adverse feature is identified on final assessment

nodes.name: Nasopharynx restaging
nodes.title: Nasopharynx: EBV-DNA-guided restaging
nodes.description: After nasopharyngeal chemoradiation, plasma EBV DNA and imaging direct whether adjuvant chemotherapy is added before surveillance.

options.label: Undetectable plasma EBV DNA, complete response
Detectable plasma EBV DNA / residual disease

nodes.name: Nasopharynx observe
nodes.title: Nasopharynx (EBV cleared): surveillance
nodes.description: Undetectable post-treatment EBV DNA with a complete response proceeds directly to surveillance.
bullets: No adjuvant chemotherapy when EBV DNA is undetectable and imaging shows a complete response
Then structured surveillance with serial plasma EBV DNA (next step)
Manage late radiation toxicity (xerostomia, hearing, endocrine)

nodes.name: Nasopharynx adjuvant chemo
nodes.title: Nasopharynx (EBV detectable): adjuvant chemotherapy
nodes.description: Detectable post-treatment EBV DNA or residual disease supports adjuvant chemotherapy before surveillance.
bullets: Adjuvant chemotherapy (e.g. gemcitabine + cisplatin, or capecitabine) for detectable EBV DNA / residual disease
Reassess distant disease before committing to adjuvant chemotherapy
Then structured surveillance with serial plasma EBV DNA (next step)
Adjuvant gemcitabine-cisplatin regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative-intent therapy.
bullets: History and physical with complete head-and-neck exam every 1-3 months in year 1, lengthening to annually by year 5
Post-treatment baseline imaging (PET-CT ~3 months after chemoradiation); further imaging for signs/symptoms
TSH every 6-12 months if the neck was irradiated; dental, speech, swallow, and smoking-cessation support
For nasopharynx - serial plasma EBV DNA; investigate new symptoms promptly
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence or metastasis is detected: go to the Recurrence / Metastatic pathway

nodes.name: Recurrent/metastatic setting
nodes.title: Recurrent / metastatic: setting
nodes.description: Distinguish an isolated, potentially salvageable locoregional recurrence from unresectable-recurrent or distant metastatic disease that needs systemic therapy.
bullets: Biopsy to confirm recurrence; restage with PET-CT to define resectability and exclude distant disease
Obtain PD-L1 CPS (and review prior platinum exposure) before selecting systemic therapy

nodes.name: Salvage local therapy
nodes.title: Locoregional recurrence: salvage therapy
nodes.description: Isolated locoregional recurrence is treated with curative intent when feasible, then surveillance.
bullets: Salvage surgery for resectable recurrence, when technically feasible
Re-irradiation (+/- concurrent systemic therapy) in previously irradiated fields for unresectable or high-risk recurrence
If salvage is not possible, treat as unresectable/metastatic with systemic therapy
Then resume structured surveillance (next step); consider clinical trials

nodes.name: R/M line of therapy
nodes.title: Recurrent / metastatic: line of therapy
nodes.description: Systemic therapy is directed by whether this is first-line disease or progression after prior platinum-based therapy.

nodes.name: R/M first-line PD-L1
nodes.title: First-line R/M: PD-L1 CPS-directed selection
nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy is selected by PD-L1 CPS and disease burden. Immunotherapy-based options for PD-L1-expressing tumors; EXTREME when immunotherapy is not suitable.

tables.title: PD-L1 CPS-directed first-line options
rows: Any CPS, higher burden / rapid progression

options.label: Any CPS, higher burden - pembrolizumab + chemotherapy

nodes.name: R/M pembrolizumab mono
nodes.title: First-line R/M: pembrolizumab monotherapy
nodes.description: PD-L1 CPS >= 1, lower-burden disease - single-agent checkpoint inhibition, then on-progression sequencing.
nodes.path: Head & Neck / Recurrent / First-line / Pembro mono
bullets: Pembrolizumab monotherapy for PD-L1 CPS >= 1 without high tumor burden or rapid progression
Add chemotherapy (see pembrolizumab + chemotherapy) if the disease becomes bulky or rapidly progressing
On progression, move to second-line therapy (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: R/M pembrolizumab + chemo
nodes.title: First-line R/M: pembrolizumab + platinum + 5-FU
nodes.description: Checkpoint inhibition combined with chemotherapy - broadly active first-line option, favored for higher tumor burden, then on-progression sequencing.
nodes.path: Head & Neck / Recurrent / First-line / Pembro + chemo
bullets: Pembrolizumab + platinum (cisplatin or carboplatin) + 5-FU, then pembrolizumab maintenance
Preferred first-line for higher tumor burden or rapid progression, across CPS levels
On progression, move to second-line therapy (next step)
Pembrolizumab + platinum + 5-FU regimen referenced below

nodes.name: R/M EXTREME
nodes.title: First-line R/M: EXTREME (platinum + 5-FU + cetuximab)
nodes.description: Chemotherapy plus cetuximab when immunotherapy is not suitable, then on-progression sequencing.
bullets: Platinum (cisplatin or carboplatin) + 5-FU + cetuximab, then cetuximab maintenance
Option when checkpoint inhibition is contraindicated (e.g. active autoimmune disease) or unavailable
On progression, move to second-line therapy (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: R/M post-platinum
nodes.title: R/M after prior platinum: checkpoint inhibitor / cetuximab
nodes.description: Progression after platinum-based therapy - checkpoint inhibition if not previously given, otherwise chemotherapy or cetuximab-based therapy, then later-line sequencing.
bullets: Nivolumab (or pembrolizumab) if a checkpoint inhibitor was not already used - improves survival vs single-agent chemotherapy
If immunotherapy already given: single-agent chemotherapy (taxane, methotrexate) or cetuximab-based therapy
On further progression, move to later-line therapy or best supportive care (next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: R/M progression
nodes.title: On progression after first-line R/M: second-line selection
nodes.description: Second-line selection after first-line progression depends on prior immunotherapy exposure.

nodes.name: R/M second-line IO
nodes.title: Second-line R/M (IO-naive): checkpoint inhibitor
nodes.description: A checkpoint inhibitor for patients who progressed on first-line chemotherapy without prior immunotherapy, then later-line sequencing.
bullets: Nivolumab (or pembrolizumab) after platinum-based first-line chemotherapy without prior immunotherapy
Improves survival vs single-agent chemotherapy in the post-platinum setting
On progression, move to later-line therapy or best supportive care (next step)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: R/M second-line chemo
nodes.title: Second-line R/M (IO-exposed): chemotherapy / cetuximab
nodes.description: Single-agent chemotherapy or cetuximab-based therapy after prior immunotherapy, then later-line sequencing.
bullets: Single-agent chemotherapy (taxane, methotrexate) or cetuximab-based therapy after prior checkpoint inhibition
Choice guided by performance status, prior agents, and toxicity
On progression, move to later-line therapy or best supportive care (next step)
Cetuximab regimen referenced below

nodes.name: R/M later line
nodes.title: Later-line R/M: further therapy vs best supportive care
nodes.description: After second-line progression, weigh a further line of therapy against best supportive care by performance status and goals of care.

options.label: Adequate performance status - further systemic therapy / trial
Poor performance status - best supportive care

nodes.name: R/M later-line therapy
nodes.title: Later-line R/M: further systemic therapy / clinical trial
nodes.description: Further single-agent therapy or a clinical trial for patients retaining adequate performance status.
bullets: Alternate single-agent chemotherapy (e.g. taxane, methotrexate) or cetuximab-based therapy not previously used
Prioritize clinical-trial enrollment where available
Reassess performance status and goals of care at each progression
Cetuximab regimen referenced below

nodes.name: R/M best supportive care
nodes.title: Later-line R/M: best supportive care
nodes.description: Best supportive and palliative care for patients with poor performance status or who choose to stop antineoplastic therapy.
bullets: Symptom-directed palliative care (pain, airway, nutrition, secretions, bleeding)
Palliative radiation for local symptoms as appropriate
Early palliative-care and hospice involvement; advance-care planning
No dose protocol - supportive-care guidance only
